premise: Overcoming orphanhood and severe scalp ailments to build a cosmetics empire and become America's first self-made female millionaire.
hook: Suffering from hair loss due to poor sanitation and lack of indoor plumbing, she formulated her own healing tonic.
key_facts: Born on a cotton plantation in Delta, Louisiana, orphaned at age seven.
Worked for decades as a washerwoman before developing hair care products for Black women.
Founded Madam C.J. Walker Manufacturing Company in 1906.
Employed thousands of women as sales agents and became a prominent philanthropist.

premise: Choosing to disobey protocol and report a nuclear warning signal as a false alarm during the height of the Cold War.
hook: Computer screens flashed with incoming US ballistic missiles, and he had minutes to decide whether to launch a retaliatory strike.
key_facts: Served as a lieutenant colonel in the Soviet Air Defense Forces in 1983.
The Oko nuclear early warning system falsely reported five American missiles launched from Montana.
Suspected a computer malfunction because the incoming count was too low for a first strike.
Reported the alert as a false alarm, averting a potential nuclear exchange.

premise: Deciding to fly a single-engine monoplane across the treacherous Atlantic Ocean without a parachute or radio.
hook: He stripped his custom aircraft of every ounce of excess weight—including the radio—to bet his life on a nonstop flight to Paris.
key_facts: Flew the custom-built Spirit of St. Louis from Roosevelt Field, New York, to Paris in May 1927.
Completed the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight in 33.5 hours.
Flew without a forward-facing windshield, relying on a periscope to see ahead.
Became an instant global aviation icon upon landing at Le Bourget Airport.

premise: Co-founding Infosys with just $250 borrowed from his wife, growing it into a global IT giant.
hook: He started a multinational tech powerhouse from a spare bedroom with a minuscule loan and a borrowed dining table.
key_facts: Started Infosys in Pune, India, in 1981 with six other software engineers.
Relied on initial seed capital provided by his wife, Sudha Murthy, from her personal savings.
Pioneered the global delivery model for software services out of India.

premise: Building a global cosmetic empire from scratch after facing systemic discrimination in the male-dominated corporate world of the 1960s.
hook: After men were promoted over her for decades, she took her life savings of $5,000 to build a company run by women, for women.
key_facts: Founded Mary Kay Cosmetics in 1963 with an initial investment of $5,000.
Pioneered a direct-sales model utilizing independent beauty consultants.
Built an enterprise generating billions in annual retail sales.

premise: Choosing not to patent the polio vaccine, ensuring it remained freely accessible globally.
hook: He was asked who owned the patent to the vaccine that saved millions, and his answer shocked the corporate world.
key_facts: Developed the first safe and effective polio vaccine in the early 1950s.
Announced the vaccine's success publicly on national radio in 1955.
Chose not to patent the discovery, stating that the patent belonged to the people.

premise: Overcoming extreme poverty and repeated failures on high-altitude expeditions to finally reach the roof of the world.
hook: He spent decades carrying heavy loads up the world's highest mountains for others, until he finally stepped onto the summit of Everest himself.
key_facts: Born into a family of yak herders in the Khumbu region of Nepal.
Participated in multiple Himalayan expeditions as a high-altitude porter and sirdar.
Reached the summit of Mount Everest alongside Edmund Hillary on May 29, 1953.

premise: Inventing a completely unorthodox, backward jumping technique that revolutionized high jumping forever.
hook: Every high jumper in the world cleared the bar facing down, until a frustrated college student decided to jump backward over his head.
key_facts: Pioneered the 'Fosbury Flop' technique at Oregon State University in the late 1960s.
Won the gold medal using his revolutionary technique at the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City.
Permanently changed how modern athletes approach the high jump event.

premise: Keeping all twenty-seven members of his crew alive for nearly two years after their ship was crushed by Antarctic ice.
hook: His ship was splintered and swallowed by Antarctic pack ice, stranding his crew on floating ice floes for 522 days with zero outside communication.
key_facts: Led the Imperial Trans-Antarctic Expedition aboard the Endurance in 1914.
Navigated a 22-foot lifeboat across 800 miles of stormy Southern Ocean seas to reach South Georgia island.
Successfully rescued every single member of his stranded expedition crew.

premise: Inventing the microwave oven after a candy bar melted in his pocket while working near a magnetron tube.
hook: He was standing next to a military radar radar tube when the peanut cluster in his shirt pocket began to bubble and cook.
key_facts: Worked as an engineer for the Raytheon Corporation during World War II.
Noticed that electromagnetic waves from a magnetron had melted a snack in his pocket.
Patented the first commercial microwave oven, known as the Radarange, in 1947.

premise: Rising from a public housing project in Brooklyn to transform a small regional coffee bean shop into Starbucks.
hook: He watched his father lose his job after a workplace injury, vowing to build a company that treated working people with dignity.
key_facts: Grew up in the Bayview housing projects in Brooklyn, New York.
Joined Starbucks as the director of marketing when it had only a handful of stores.
Acquired the company in 1987 and expanded it into a global cafe franchise.

premise: Deciding to test wing-warping mechanics inspired by observing birds in flight to achieve controlled powered flight.
hook: While watching pigeons maneuver in flight, two bicycle mechanics realized the secret to human flight was not brute engine power, but twisting wings.
key_facts: Studied bird flight patterns to develop the concept of wing-warping for lateral control.
Conducted glider experiments in Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, between 1900 and 1903.
Achieved the first sustained, controlled powered heavier-than-air flight on December 17, 1903.

premise: Overcoming a destructive avalanche and severe injuries to become the first woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest.
hook: An avalanche crushed her base camp tent under feet of snow, but she refused to turn back until she stood on top of the world.
key_facts: Formed the Ladies Climbing Club in Japan in 1969 to facilitate women's mountaineering expeditions.
Survived an avalanche at Camp II during her 1975 Everest ascent.
Reached the summit of Mount Everest on May 16, 1975.
